spots.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral, Fortaleza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The St. Joseph's Cathedral also called Metropolitan Cathedral of St. Joseph is a Catholic church, home of the Archdiocese of Fortaleza, located in Fortaleza in Brazil. The present church was built on the site of the old church.

spots.name: Ponte dos Ingleses
spots.summary: Construction of this pier started in 1923, but it has never functioned as a port as intended. Its sunset view is reputedly the best in the city.

spots.name: Theatro José de Alencar
spots.summary: The Theatro José de Alencar is a Brazilian theater located in the city of Fortaleza, Ceará.

spots.name: Praia de Iracema
spots.summary: Praia de Iracema is a beach and a neighborhood located in the Brazilian city of Fortaleza in the state of Ceará. Its name comes from the character Iracema that gives name to a famous novel by the cearense writer José de Alencar.

spots.name: Praça do Ferreira
spots.summary: The main city square named after the pharmacist Antônio Rodrigues Ferreira and is surrounded by stores, restaurants, a movie theater and plenty of benches. Inaugurated in 1829, it has been rebuilt several times and is surrounded by many buildings of historical importance. The square of today features a time column and a small garden, just like the original version.

spots.summary: An all too common sight in South America; Fortaleza has a beautiful railway station... but traffic ended in 1975.

spots.name: Seminário da Prainha
spots.summary: A Catholic seminary with a neoclassical church from the 19th century. If you're interested in the city's local religious history or want to do some genealogical studies, this is the right place to visit.

spots.name: Palácio da Luz

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palácio da Luz was the former head office of the government of Ceará state, Brazil. It was built at the end of the 18th century, with the help of indigenous labour, and it was acquired by the Imperial Government in 1814. It now is the headquarters of the Academia Cearense de Letras.

spots.name: Estoril
spots.summary: This mansion, built in 1925 as Vila Morena, and later used as a casino, a restaurant (when its current name was applied) and a rather political bar, is of peculiar architecture. It was virtually rebuilt in the 1990s, and is undergoing another refurbishment to be used for public cultural arrangements.

spots.name: Praça José de Alencar (Fortaleza)
spots.summary: Plenty of greenery and the place to catch the city's best street performers. The square, which used to functioned as a bus station, is today frequented by small market stalls and food carts. On the southern side of this square is the eponymous theater building.

spots.name: Museu do Ceará
spots.summary: In a late 19th-century seat of state government. Explains the history of the state of Ceará and its capital.

spots.name: Castelão
spots.summary: Estádio Governador Plácido Castelo, also known as the Castelão or Gigante da Boa Vista, is a football stadium that was inaugurated on November 11, 1973, in Fortaleza, Ceará, Brazil. With a maximum capacity of 57,867 spectators it is the sixth largest stadium in the country.

spots.name: Dragão do Mar
spots.summary: The square at Rua Dragão do Mar is culturally a very lively place. Several artisans are selling their work there, musicians are performing and there are several bars and restaurants with international cuisine as well as night clubs of different styles. Then there's also the cultural center, described below.

spots.name: Mini Siará
spots.summary: More cute than really interesting, this tiny museum has about 25 scale models of Fortaleza's colonial buildings, and also a couple of scale landscapes.

spots.name: Museu de Arte e Cultura Popular

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Located in an old prison, now the Centro de Turismo, along with a handicraft market and a tourist information. Displays many fine examples of folk art as well as boats and other cultural relics.

spots.name: Iracema Statue
spots.summary: Also known as the Guardian of Iracema, this statue was constructed to honor the author José de Alencar. The statue depicts the protagonist in his novel Iracema. Another one stands in Messejena Lake in the south of the city.
